🇲🇽🏭 <u>Car Sales: Best January–September on Record</u>

INEGI: Mexico sold 129,288 new light vehicles in September, up 8.0% year on year and the seventh straight month of growth. From January to September the total is 1,144,002 units, up 5.0%, beating 2016's record pace by 21,860 vehicles (via El Economista).

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Slim Wants 700 Apartments in Puebla's UNESCO-Protected Center</u>

Grupo Carso and Puebla mayor Pepe Chedraui unveiled a roughly 4-billion-peso plan for Paseo de San Francisco: 700 apartments for sale and rent, two levels of shopping corridors and underground parking up to four floors deep. It sits on 45,000 m² inside a World Heritage historic center where INAH protects 2,619 buildings. Slim calls them "low-cost housing" and denies gentrification. Puebla's culture secretary Fritz Glockner isn't convinced: "This isn't intervening in a little garden."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Chiapas: 57 Arrested in Joint Federal-State Sweep</u>

Federal and state forces ran joint operations across Chiapas: 57 people arrested, plus 9 firearms, 157 rounds, 5,512 doses of drugs and 12 vehicles seized. After a shooting in Tuxtla Gutiérrez's Las Granjas neighborhood that killed three, investigators arrested 34 people. Among them were the alleged cell leader "el Bebé" and the alleged mastermind. In Tapachula, 16 alleged members of "Los Cuatetes" were taken in, and a Salvadoran Barrio 18 member wanted at home for multiple homicides was caught in Tuxtla.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>UN: Searching for the Disappeared Is the State's Job, Not Mothers'</u>

UN human rights experts warn that women searching for disappeared relatives in Mexico face "alarming" violence, which in the worst cases ends in their own disappearance or murder, amid "almost total impunity." Their message to the Mexican State is clear: family participation is a right, but the search is its responsibility, and it "must assume it fully and cannot shift it onto the shoulders of families."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>FGR Won't Drop the 948-Million-Peso Next Energy Case</u>

A federal judge in Aguascalientes refused to try five former officials of PAN governor Teresa Jiménez's old city administration over a 948-million-peso solar contract awarded to Next Energy. The FGR is appealing. It says the judge "left out legal elements," and lines of investigation into the use of federal money and possible financial schemes stay open.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>VW Puebla: 13.16% Raise, 611 Workers Rehired, No Strike</u>

The independent union at Volkswagen's Cuautlancingo plant said "no" to 10% in September and held the line. On October 2, Sitiavw and VW México signed a preliminary deal: a 13.16% global increase over 24 months, a one-time payment of 17,800 pesos, and the rehiring of the 611 technicians the company laid off last month. No strike, no surrender. The deal now goes back to the rank and file for a vote.

🇲🇽🏛️ 17,000 archaeological pieces returned to Mexico since 2018, ten times more than under previous governments. — Claudia Curiel de Icaza, Secretary of Culture In the last two years alone, 5,686 pieces were restituted with the Foreign Ministry, "a reflection of a different vocation and commitment to our memory and heritage." Another 520 million pesos went to the conservation of 74 archaeological zones and 34 museums.

🇲🇽⚖️ "It cannot be that cases of child abuse come out on social media, and that the networks do nothing." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 2, 2026 On Oct 1, two adult brothers, both former students, entered Secondary School No. 13 in Torreón, Coahuila, and attacked staff and students with knives. A member of the school's leadership was killed and four people were injured. Investigators found similarities with a recent case in Querétaro and two or three others involving communication over social media. Sheinbaum formed a working group led by Legal Counsel Luisa María Alcalde, with experts from UNAM and IPN. The goal is a decree next week obliging platforms to take down content that incites violence and report it, defined clearly "so they don't border on censorship."

🇲🇽🕊️ "Never again, never again a repression by the State against a social movement." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 2, 2026 Today marks 58 years since the October 2, 1968 massacre of students in the Plaza de Tlatelolco. Sheinbaum opened the mañanera with "October 2 is not forgotten" and recalled that two years ago, on taking office, her government published a statement in the Official Gazette naming then-president Gustavo Díaz Ordaz, commander of the armed forces, as the main person responsible, as he himself acknowledged after leaving office.
